la:verb:perhorresco.html:
pĕr-horresco, rui, 3,
v. inch. n. and a.
Neutr., to tremble or shudder greatly (class.): toto corpore perhorresco,: recordatione consulatūs vestri,: clamore perhorruit Aetne,trembled, shook,: latumque perhorruit aequor (ventorum jactatibus),.—
Act., to shudder greatly at, to have a great horror of any thing (class.): hanc tantam religionem non perhorrescis?: vexationem virginum Vestalium perhorresco,: Bosporum,.

la:verb:perhorreo.html:
pĕr-horrĕo, ui, 2, v. a.,
to tremble or shudder greatly at, to have a great horror of any thing (post-class.): horum tela perhorrebimus, Mai.

la:adj:perhonorificus.gloss: very honorific (that shows or confers great honour)
senses: very honorific (that shows or confers great honour)
la:adj:perhonorificus.html:
pĕr-hŏnōrĭfĭcus, a, um, adj.
Thatdoes one much honor, very honorable: con salutatio forensis perhonorifica,. 18, 1: discessus,.—
That shows much honor to another, very respectful: collega in me perhonorificus,.—Adv.: pĕrhŏnōrĭfĭcē, very respectfully, .

la:adj:perhumanus.html:
pĕr-hūmānus, a, um, adj.,
very kind, very courteous, very polite (class.): sermo,: epistula,. —Adv.: pĕrhūmānĭter, very kindly, very politely: scribere ad aliquem,.

la:verb:perhibeo.gloss: to hold out, extend; present, produce, bestow, afford, grant, give
senses: to hold out, extend; present, produce, bestow, afford, grant, give
la:verb:perhibeo.html:
pĕr-hĭbĕo, ui, ĭtum, 2, v. a.
habeo
,
to hold out, extend, present, produce, bestow, grant, give, afford; to attribute, ascribe, assign, etc.
In gen. (mostly ante-class. and post-Aug.; cf.: edo, exhibeo): operam rei publicae fortem atque strenuam, Cato ap. : magnanimitatis exemplum,: testimonium,to bear witness,; ; ; : ut testimonium perhiberet de lumine,; , 10, 2 fin.; et saep.: in causā universorum creditorum, qui sine eo, quem Caecilius suo nomine perhiberet, facile causam communem sustinerent,to bring forward, furnish,: magnam auctoritatem huic animali perhibet Nigidius,attributes,: alicui rei palmam,to give the preference,: cui (Vettonicae) tanta vis perhibetur, ut, etc.,; : ut rebus praecipuis honos in primis perhibeatur,.—
In partic., to say, assert any thing; to call, name any thing (mostly poet.; in Cic. very rare, perh. only three times; cf. Madv. Opusc. Acad. p. 200, and ad ): vento quem perhibent Graium genus aëra linguā, Enn. ap. Prob. ad (Ann. v. 149 Vahl.); cf.: id quod nostri caelum memorant, Grai perhibent aethera, Pac. ap. Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 71 Rib.): est locus Hesperiam quam mortales perhibebant, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 23 Vahl.): omnes corde patrem perhibent, id. ap. Don. ad ( ib.): Jove propagatus est, ut perhibent, Tantalus, Poët. ap. ; so, ut perhibent viri,; and: Electrā, ut Graii perhibent, Atlantide cretus,: bene qui coniciet, vatem hunc perhibebo optimum, Cic. poët. Div. 2, 5, 12.—With acc. and inf.: fortunam insanam esse perhibent philosophi, Pac. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 104 Rib.).—In pass.: sophiam sapientia quae perhibetur, Enn. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 227 Vahl.): sane ego me nolo fortem perhiberi virum, Plaut. Fragm. ap. : quis me inprobior perhibeatur esse,: montes, qui esse aurei perhibentur,are said to be,: Tyndaridae fratres, qui nuntii fuisse perhibentur,: his (Romulus) dicitur ... perhibetur ceteris praestitisse,: nec minus est Spartiates Agesilaus ille perhibendus,to be named, cited,.
